title: Three requirements of true obedience
source_text: XXIII. Ut autem istud clarius innotescat, observandum est ad hoc, ut obedientia nostra vera & sincera sit, tria praecipue requiri. Primum est ut praestetur non tantum corpore & opere externo, sed interno quoque animi affectu. Neque enim quicquam prodest ea facere quae lex jubet, nisi id fiat ex Dei amore, & voluntatis illius implendae ac gloriae ejus promovendae studio. Ut nec satis est quendam affectum Deo obsequendi habere, nisi mandata ejus, quum res id postulat, ipso opere compleantur. Praeterea non sufficit ad veram obedientiam ut quaedam Dei mandata, reliquis neglectis, servemus: sed necesse est ut omnibus legis Divinae praeceptis nos serio subjiciamus, illaque, cum sese offert occasio, implere studeamus. Denique debet esse obedientia nostra constans & perseverans: Nec satis est Deo ad tempus obsequi, sed in ejus obsequio, tam per res adversas quam per res secundas, ad finem usque perseverandum est.
pass_a_gloss: XXIII. But that this may become clearer, it must be observed that for this, that our obedience be true & sincere, three things chiefly are required. The first is that it be rendered not only with the body & outward work, but also with the inward affection of the mind. For it profits nothing to do those things which the law commands, unless it be done out of love for God, & out of zeal for fulfilling his will & promoting his glory. As neither is it enough to have a certain affection of obeying God, unless his commandments, when the matter requires it, are carried out in the work itself. Moreover it does not suffice for true obedience that we keep certain commandments of God, the rest neglected: but it is necessary that we seriously submit ourselves to all the precepts of the Divine law, & strive to fulfil them, when occasion offers itself. Lastly our obedience ought to be constant & persevering: Nor is it enough to obey God for a time, but in his obedience, through adverse things as well as through prosperous things, one must persevere right to the end.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIII. To make this clearer, note that three things above all are needed for our obedience to be true and sincere. First, it must be given not only with the body and outward action but with the inner affection of the mind as well. Doing what the law commands profits nothing unless it springs from love of God and from zeal to carry out his will and advance his glory. Equally, a certain wish to obey God is not enough unless his commandments are actually carried out in deed when the situation calls for it.

Second, true obedience is not satisfied by keeping some of God's commandments while neglecting the rest. We must earnestly submit to every precept of the divine law and try to fulfil each one as occasions arise. Third, our obedience must be steady and lasting. Obeying God for a while is not enough; we have to persevere in obeying him to the end, in hard times as in good ones.

lemmas.gloss: also with the inward affection of the mind

choices.why: The marks of the obedience Le Blanc grants to believers, which Scripture calls 'perfect' in the sense of integrity.
